text: Intubate for a GCS of {{8}} or less.
extra: GCS: eyes 4, verbal 5, motor 6. Motor score is the most prognostic.
points: GCS: eyes 4, verbal 5, motor 6. Motor score is the most prognostic.

text: Beck's triad of tamponade: {{hypotension}}, {{JVD}}, and {{muffled heart sounds}}.
extra: Treat with pericardial window or sternotomy; pericardiocentesis only temporizes.
points: Treat with pericardial window or sternotomy; pericardiocentesis only temporizes.

text: Neck zone II runs from the {{cricoid cartilage}} to the {{angle of the mandible}}.
extra: Zone I: clavicle to cricoid. Zone III: angle of mandible to skull base.
points: Zone III: angle of mandible to skull base.

text: Blunt aortic injury occurs most often at the {{ligamentum arteriosum}}, just distal to the left subclavian.
extra: Treat with impulse control (beta blocker) and then TEVAR.
points: Treat with impulse control (beta blocker) and then TEVAR.

text: The lethal triad in trauma: {{hypothermia}}, {{acidosis}}, {{coagulopathy}}.
extra: Basis for damage control surgery: control bleeding and contamination, resuscitate, return later.
points: Basis for damage control surgery: control bleeding and contamination, resuscitate, return later.

text: Massive transfusion targets a plasma:platelet:RBC ratio of {{1:1:1}}.
extra: Balanced resuscitation reduces death from exsanguination (PROPPR).
points: Balanced resuscitation reduces death from exsanguination (PROPPR).

text: Posterior knee dislocation: evaluate the {{popliteal artery}}; an ABI under {{0.9}} needs CT angiography.
extra: Hard signs of vascular injury go to the operating room.
points: Hard signs of vascular injury go to the operating room.

text: Epidural hematoma: {{middle meningeal artery}}, lens shaped, lucid interval.
extra: Subdural hematoma: bridging veins, crescent shaped, crosses suture lines.
points: Subdural hematoma: bridging veins, crescent shaped, crosses suture lines.

text: Cushing's reflex: {{hypertension}} and {{bradycardia}} with irregular breathing.
extra: A sign of raised intracranial pressure and impending herniation.
points: A sign of raised intracranial pressure and impending herniation.

text: Blood at the urethral meatus: get a {{retrograde urethrogram}} before placing a Foley.
extra: Other signs: high-riding prostate, perineal hematoma, pelvic fracture.
points: Other signs: high-riding prostate, perineal hematoma, pelvic fracture.

text: Seat belt sign with a Chance fracture suggests {{small bowel or mesenteric}} injury.
extra: A Chance fracture is a flexion-distraction injury of the thoracolumbar spine.
points: A Chance fracture is a flexion-distraction injury of the thoracolumbar spine.

text: Neurogenic shock: hypotension with {{bradycardia}} and warm extremities.
extra: Loss of sympathetic tone from injury above T6. Treat with fluids then vasopressors.
points: Loss of sympathetic tone from injury above T6.

text: Cardiogenic shock: cardiac output {{low}}, wedge pressure {{high}}, SVR {{high}}.
extra: Hypovolemic shock: low output, low wedge, high SVR.
points: Hypovolemic shock: low output, low wedge, high SVR.

text: Septic shock (early): cardiac output {{high}}, SVR {{low}}.
extra: Distributive shock. Mixed venous saturation is often high.
points: Mixed venous saturation is often high.

text: ARDS (Berlin): PaO2/FiO2 under {{300}}, bilateral infiltrates, within one week, not cardiac.
extra: Mild 200 to 300, moderate 100 to 200, severe under 100.
points: Mild 200 to 300, moderate 100 to 200, severe under 100.

text: Prone positioning improves survival in ARDS when P/F is under {{150}}.
extra: Prone for at least 16 hours per day (PROSEVA).
points: Prone for at least 16 hours per day (PROSEVA).

text: Vasopressin vasoconstricts through {{V1}} receptors; {{V2}} receptors reabsorb water in the collecting duct.
extra: DDAVP is V2 selective and releases vWF and factor VIII.
points: DDAVP is V2 selective and releases vWF and factor VIII.

text: Refractory hypotension in a patient on chronic steroids: give {{hydrocortisone}}.
extra: Adrenal insufficiency: hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia.
points: Adrenal insufficiency: hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia.

text: One gram of hemoglobin carries {{1.34}} mL of oxygen.
extra: O2 content = Hgb x 1.34 x SaO2 + 0.003 x PaO2. Delivery = cardiac output x content.
points: O2 content = Hgb x 1.34 x SaO2 + 0.003 x PaO2.

text: Most common cause of fever in the first 48 hours after surgery (classic teaching): {{atelectasis}}.
extra: Wind, water, wound, walking, wonder drugs. Very early high fever with wound changes: think necrotizing infection.
points: Wind, water, wound, walking, wonder drugs.
Very early high fever with wound changes: think necrotizing infection.

text: Total body water is about {{60}}% of body weight in men: 2/3 intracellular, 1/3 extracellular.
extra: Extracellular: 3/4 interstitial, 1/4 plasma.

text: Lactated Ringer's contains sodium {{130}}, potassium 4, calcium 2.7, chloride 109, lactate 28.
extra: Normal saline: sodium 154, chloride 154.

text: Large volumes of normal saline cause {{hyperchloremic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis}}.
extra: Use balanced crystalloids for large-volume resuscitation.
points: Use balanced crystalloids for large-volume resuscitation.

text: Correct chronic hyponatremia no faster than {{8}} to 10 mEq/L per 24 hours.
extra: Too fast causes osmotic demyelination. Correcting hypernatremia too fast causes cerebral edema.
points: Correcting hypernatremia too fast causes cerebral edema.

text: Refractory hypokalemia: first correct {{magnesium}}.
extra: Low magnesium also causes refractory hypocalcemia.
points: Low magnesium also causes refractory hypocalcemia.

text: First treatment of hypercalcemic crisis: {{normal saline}} hydration.
extra: Then calcitonin and bisphosphonates. Avoid thiazides.

text: Maintenance fluids by the 4-2-1 rule: {{4}} mL/kg/h for the first 10 kg, 2 for the next 10, 1 thereafter.
extra: A 70 kg adult needs about 110 mL/h.
points: A 70 kg adult needs about 110 mL/h.

text: Vomiting or NG suction causes {{hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis}} with paradoxical aciduria.
extra: Treat with normal saline and potassium.
points: Treat with normal saline and potassium.

text: The GI fluid with the most potassium is {{saliva}}; the most bicarbonate is {{pancreatic fluid}}.
extra: High-output pancreatic or small bowel fistulas cause non-gap acidosis.
points: High-output pancreatic or small bowel fistulas cause non-gap acidosis.

text: Calories per gram: fat {{9}}, protein 4, carbohydrate 4.
extra: IV dextrose gives 3.4 kcal/g.

text: A respiratory quotient above 1 means {{overfeeding}}; 0.7 means fat use or starvation.
extra: Overfeeding raises CO2 production and can impair ventilator weaning.
points: Overfeeding raises CO2 production and can impair ventilator weaning.

text: Fuel of the colonocyte: {{short-chain fatty acids (butyrate)}}; fuel of the enterocyte: {{glutamine}}.
extra: Diversion colitis is treated with short-chain fatty acid enemas.
points: Diversion colitis is treated with short-chain fatty acid enemas.

text: Half-life of prealbumin: {{2 days}}; albumin: about 20 days.
extra: Prealbumin tracks short-term nutritional change.

text: Chromium deficiency causes {{hyperglycemia}} and neuropathy.
extra: Zinc deficiency: poor wound healing, rash, hair loss. Copper: pancytopenia.
points: Zinc deficiency: poor wound healing, rash, hair loss.

text: Zinc deficiency causes {{poor wound healing}}, perioral rash, and hair loss.
extra: Common with high-output fistulas and long-term TPN.
points: Common with high-output fistulas and long-term TPN.

text: Hemophilia A is deficiency of factor {{VIII}}; it prolongs the {{PTT}}.
extra: X-linked. Hemophilia B is factor IX. Hemarthrosis is typical.

text: The clotting factor with the shortest half-life is factor {{VII}}.
extra: This is why PT/INR rises first in liver failure and with warfarin.
points: This is why PT/INR rises first in liver failure and with warfarin.

text: Vitamin K-dependent factors: {{II, VII, IX, X}}, plus proteins C and S.
extra: Warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase.
points: Warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase.

text: Most common inherited hypercoagulable state: {{factor V Leiden}}.
extra: It causes resistance to activated protein C.
points: It causes resistance to activated protein C.

text: Cryoprecipitate is rich in {{fibrinogen}}, factor VIII, vWF, and factor XIII.
extra: Give for fibrinogen under 100 to 150 in a bleeding patient.
points: Give for fibrinogen under 100 to 150 in a bleeding patient.

text: Uremic platelet dysfunction is treated with {{DDAVP}}.
extra: Dialysis also helps. Platelet count is normal; function is impaired.
points: Platelet count is normal; function is impaired.

text: Heparin potentiates {{antithrombin III}} and is reversed with {{protamine}}.
extra: 1 mg protamine per 100 units of heparin. Protamine reverses LMWH only partly.
points: 1 mg protamine per 100 units of heparin.

text: Warfarin skin necrosis occurs with {{protein C}} deficiency.
extra: Protein C has a short half-life, causing a transient hypercoagulable state. Bridge with heparin.
points: Protein C has a short half-life, causing a transient hypercoagulable state.

text: TRALI is caused by {{donor antibodies}} against recipient leukocytes.
extra: Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours of transfusion. Supportive care.
points: Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours of transfusion.

text: Most common organism in surgical site infection: {{Staphylococcus aureus}}.
extra: Most common gram-negative in SSI: E. coli.
points: Most common gram-negative in SSI: E. coli.

text: Prophylactic antibiotics are given within {{60 minutes}} before incision.
extra: Stop within 24 hours. Redose for long cases or major blood loss.
points: Redose for long cases or major blood loss.

text: Most common organism in central line infection: {{coagulase-negative staphylococci}}.
extra: Staph epidermidis. Remove the line for S. aureus, Candida, or sepsis.
points: Remove the line for S. aureus, Candida, or sepsis.

text: Clindamycin is added in toxin-mediated infections because it {{inhibits toxin synthesis}}.
extra: It blocks the 50S ribosome. Used with penicillin for group A strep and Clostridium.
points: Used with penicillin for group A strep and Clostridium.

text: Candidemia: start an {{echinocandin}}, remove central lines, and get an eye exam.
extra: Micafungin or caspofungin. Treat for 14 days after the first negative culture.
points: Treat for 14 days after the first negative culture.

text: Elective colectomy with no spillage is a {{clean-contaminated}} wound.
extra: Approximate infection rates: clean 2%, clean-contaminated 3 to 5%, contaminated 5 to 10%, dirty 30%.
points: Approximate infection rates: clean 2%, clean-contaminated 3 to 5%, contaminated 5 to 10%, dirty 30%.

text: Vancomycin binds {{D-ala-D-ala}} cell wall precursors.
extra: VRE changes the target to D-ala-D-lac; treat with linezolid or daptomycin.
points: VRE changes the target to D-ala-D-lac; treat with linezolid or daptomycin.

text: Malignant hyperthermia is a defect of the {{ryanodine receptor}}.
extra: Triggers: succinylcholine and volatile anesthetics. Treat with dantrolene.

text: Succinylcholine is avoided in burns, crush injury, and denervation because of {{hyperkalemia}}.
extra: It is the only depolarizing muscle relaxant. Also a trigger for malignant hyperthermia.
points: It is the only depolarizing muscle relaxant.
Also a trigger for malignant hyperthermia.

text: A lower MAC means a {{more}} potent inhaled anesthetic.
extra: MAC is the alveolar concentration at which 50% of patients do not move to incision.
points: MAC is the alveolar concentration at which 50% of patients do not move to incision.

text: Etomidate's main drawback is {{adrenal suppression}}.
extra: Ketamine preserves blood pressure and bronchodilates. Propofol causes hypotension.
points: Ketamine preserves blood pressure and bronchodilates.

text: Maximum lidocaine dose: {{5}} mg/kg plain, {{7}} mg/kg with epinephrine.
extra: 1% lidocaine is 10 mg/mL. Toxicity: perioral numbness, seizures, arrhythmia. Treat with lipid emulsion.

text: Local anesthetics work poorly in infected tissue because of {{acidosis}}.
extra: The ionized form cannot cross the nerve membrane.
points: The ionized form cannot cross the nerve membrane.

text: Meperidine's metabolite {{normeperidine}} causes seizures.
extra: It accumulates in renal failure. Avoid with MAO inhibitors.

text: Order of cell arrival in a wound: platelets, {{neutrophils}}, {{macrophages}}, fibroblasts.
extra: Macrophages are essential. Fibroblasts dominate by day 5.

text: A wound reaches at most {{80%}} of original tensile strength, at about {{8 weeks}}.
extra: Remodeling continues for a year.

text: Early wound collagen is type {{III}}; it is replaced by type {{I}}.
extra: Type I is the most abundant collagen. Type IV is basement membrane.
points: Type I is the most abundant collagen.

text: Vitamin {{C}} is needed for hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen.
extra: Deficiency causes scurvy and poor wound healing.
points: Deficiency causes scurvy and poor wound healing.

text: Vitamin {{A}} reverses the effect of steroids on wound healing.
extra: Steroids inhibit macrophages and collagen synthesis.
points: Steroids inhibit macrophages and collagen synthesis.

text: The strength layer of the bowel wall is the {{submucosa}}.
extra: It holds the most collagen. Anastomoses are weakest at days 3 to 5.
points: Anastomoses are weakest at days 3 to 5.

text: A keloid extends {{beyond}} the original wound; a hypertrophic scar stays within it.
extra: Keloids: darker skin, autosomal dominant. Treat with steroid injection, silicone, radiation.
points: Treat with steroid injection, silicone, radiation.

text: Wound contraction is driven by {{myofibroblasts}}.
extra: Epithelialization proceeds at 1 to 2 mm per day.
points: Epithelialization proceeds at 1 to 2 mm per day.

text: Most common breast mass in women under 30: {{fibroadenoma}}.
extra: Mobile, rubbery, well circumscribed. Popcorn calcifications when old.

text: Most common cause of bloody nipple discharge: {{intraductal papilloma}}.
extra: Still exclude cancer. Treat with duct excision.

text: Long thoracic nerve injury causes {{winged scapula}}.
extra: It supplies serratus anterior. Thoracodorsal nerve supplies latissimus dorsi.

text: The nerve most often injured in axillary dissection is the {{intercostobrachial}} nerve.
extra: It causes numbness of the medial upper arm.
points: It causes numbness of the medial upper arm.

text: BRCA1 raises the risk of breast and {{ovarian}} cancer; BRCA2 adds {{male breast}} cancer.
extra: BRCA2 also raises pancreatic and prostate cancer risk.
points: BRCA2 also raises pancreatic and prostate cancer risk.

text: Tamoxifen raises the risk of {{endometrial cancer}} and venous thromboembolism.
extra: Aromatase inhibitors are for postmenopausal women and cause bone loss.
points: Aromatase inhibitors are for postmenopausal women and cause bone loss.

text: Trastuzumab's key toxicity is {{cardiotoxicity}}.
extra: Targets HER2. Usually reversible. Monitor with echocardiography.

text: LCIS is a {{marker of risk in both breasts}}, not a lesion needing negative margins.
extra: Manage with surveillance and chemoprevention. Pleomorphic LCIS is excised.

text: Inflammatory breast cancer: {{neoadjuvant chemotherapy}}, then modified radical mastectomy, then radiation.
extra: Peau d'orange from dermal lymphatic invasion. Staged T4d.
points: Peau d'orange from dermal lymphatic invasion.

text: Phyllodes tumor: wide excision with margins of at least {{1 cm}}; no node sampling.
extra: Spreads by blood, not lymphatics.

text: Paget's disease of the nipple signals underlying {{DCIS or invasive cancer}}.
extra: Scaly, eczematous nipple. Diagnose with full-thickness biopsy.

text: Most common thyroid cancer: {{papillary}}; it spreads by {{lymphatics}}.
extra: Psammoma bodies, Orphan Annie nuclei. Excellent prognosis.

text: Follicular thyroid cancer spreads {{hematogenously}} and cannot be diagnosed by FNA.
extra: Diagnosis needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology.
points: Diagnosis needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology.

text: Medullary thyroid cancer arises from {{parafollicular C cells}} and secretes calcitonin.
extra: Amyloid on pathology. Associated with MEN2A and 2B (RET).

text: MEN1: {{parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary}}.
extra: Menin gene. Parathyroid hyperplasia is the most common and first manifestation.
points: Parathyroid hyperplasia is the most common and first manifestation.

text: MEN2A: medullary thyroid cancer, {{pheochromocytoma}}, and {{parathyroid hyperplasia}}.
extra: MEN2B: medullary thyroid cancer, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus. Both RET.
points: MEN2B: medullary thyroid cancer, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus.

text: Injury to the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve causes loss of {{high pitch}} and voice fatigue.
extra: It supplies cricothyroid and runs with the superior thyroid artery.
points: It supplies cricothyroid and runs with the superior thyroid artery.

text: Intraoperative PTH should fall by at least {{50}}% ten minutes after excision.
extra: Miami criterion. PTH half-life is 3 to 5 minutes.

text: Most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism: {{single adenoma}}.
extra: About 85%. Hyperplasia about 10 to 15%, carcinoma under 1%.

text: Screening test for primary hyperaldosteronism: {{aldosterone-to-renin ratio}}.
extra: Conn's: hypertension and hypokalemia. Adrenal vein sampling lateralizes before surgery.
points: Adrenal vein sampling lateralizes before surgery.

text: Biochemical test for pheochromocytoma: {{plasma free metanephrines}}.
extra: Or 24-hour urine metanephrines. Do not biopsy.

text: Resect an adrenal incidentaloma if it is {{functional}} or larger than {{4 cm}}.
extra: Work-up: metanephrines, dexamethasone suppression test, aldosterone:renin if hypertensive.
points: Work-up: metanephrines, dexamethasone suppression test, aldosterone:renin if hypertensive.

text: Barrett's esophagus is intestinal metaplasia and predisposes to {{adenocarcinoma}}.
extra: Goblet cells on biopsy. High-grade dysplasia: endoscopic ablation or resection.
points: High-grade dysplasia: endoscopic ablation or resection.

text: The esophagus has no {{serosa}}.
extra: This makes anastomoses less secure and lets tumors spread early.
points: This makes anastomoses less secure and lets tumors spread early.

text: Boerhaave's perforation is usually in the {{left posterolateral distal}} esophagus.
extra: Most common site of iatrogenic perforation: at the cricopharyngeus.
points: Most common site of iatrogenic perforation: at the cricopharyngeus.

text: The gastric conduit after esophagectomy is supplied by the {{right gastroepiploic artery}}.
extra: The left gastric and short gastrics are divided.
points: The left gastric and short gastrics are divided.

text: Alkali ingestion causes {{liquefactive}} necrosis; acid causes coagulative necrosis.
extra: Alkali injury is deeper. No NG tube blindly, no neutralizing, no induced vomiting.
points: No NG tube blindly, no neutralizing, no induced vomiting.

text: Type II paraesophageal hernia: GE junction {{in normal position}} with the fundus herniated.
extra: Type I sliding (most common). Type III mixed. Type IV contains other organs.

text: Type I gastric ulcer is on the {{lesser curvature}} with normal or low acid.
extra: Types II (with duodenal ulcer) and III (prepyloric) have high acid.
points: Types II (with duodenal ulcer) and III (prepyloric) have high acid.

text: Parietal cells secrete {{acid and intrinsic factor}}; chief cells secrete pepsinogen.
extra: G cells in the antrum secrete gastrin. D cells secrete somatostatin.
points: G cells in the antrum secrete gastrin.

text: First treatment of dumping syndrome: {{dietary change}}.
extra: Small, low-carbohydrate, high-protein meals; separate liquids. Octreotide if refractory.
points: Small, low-carbohydrate, high-protein meals; separate liquids.

text: First-line treatment of gastric MALT lymphoma: {{H. pylori eradication}}.
extra: Most low-grade lesions regress with triple therapy.
points: Most low-grade lesions regress with triple therapy.

text: Gastric cancer resection should retrieve at least {{16}} lymph nodes.
extra: D2 lymphadenectomy with negative margins. Perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT) for locally advanced disease.
points: Perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT) for locally advanced disease.

text: Left supraclavicular node from gastric cancer: {{Virchow's node}}.
extra: Krukenberg: ovary. Sister Mary Joseph: umbilicus. Blumer's shelf: rectal shelf.

text: Internal hernia after Roux-en-Y bypass occurs through {{Petersen's space}} or the mesenteric defects.
extra: Swirl sign on CT. Explore early.

text: Most common cause of small bowel obstruction in adults with prior surgery: {{adhesions}}.
extra: Without prior surgery: hernia. Then tumors.

text: Vitamin B12 and bile salts are absorbed in the {{terminal ileum}}.
extra: Iron: duodenum. Folate: jejunum.

text: Meckel's diverticulum in children most often presents with {{painless lower GI bleeding}}.
extra: Ectopic gastric mucosa. In adults: obstruction. True diverticulum from the vitelline duct.
points: True diverticulum from the vitelline duct.

text: Crohn's disease most commonly involves the {{terminal ileum}}.
extra: Transmural, skip lesions, creeping fat. Resect only to grossly normal margins.
points: Resect only to grossly normal margins.

text: Carcinoid syndrome from a gut primary requires {{liver metastases}}.
extra: Flushing, diarrhea, right-sided valve disease. Urine 5-HIAA. Treat with octreotide.

text: In gallstone ileus the stone lodges in the {{terminal ileum}}.
extra: Pneumobilia on imaging. Remove the stone through a proximal enterotomy.
points: Remove the stone through a proximal enterotomy.

text: Colon cancer resection requires at least {{12}} lymph nodes.
extra: Fewer nodes means inadequate staging.

text: Average-risk colorectal cancer screening starts at age {{45}}.
extra: First-degree relative: start at 40 or 10 years before their diagnosis.
points: First-degree relative: start at 40 or 10 years before their diagnosis.

text: Lynch syndrome is caused by {{mismatch repair}} gene mutations.
extra: MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2. Microsatellite instability. Endometrial cancer is the most common extracolonic tumor.
points: Endometrial cancer is the most common extracolonic tumor.

text: FAP is caused by the {{APC}} gene on chromosome 5q.
extra: Near 100% cancer risk. Also duodenal cancer and desmoid tumors.
points: Also duodenal cancer and desmoid tumors.

text: The watershed area most prone to colonic ischemia is the {{splenic flexure}}.
extra: Griffith's point. Sudeck's point is at the rectosigmoid.
points: Sudeck's point is at the rectosigmoid.

text: Ogilvie's syndrome failing conservative care or with cecum over {{12 cm}}: give {{neostigmine}}.
extra: Monitor for bradycardia and keep atropine ready. Then colonoscopic decompression.
points: Monitor for bradycardia and keep atropine ready.

text: Hinchey III is {{purulent}} peritonitis; Hinchey IV is {{feculent}} peritonitis.
extra: I: pericolic abscess. II: pelvic or distant abscess.

text: Chronic anal fissure is usually in the {{posterior midline}}; surgery is lateral internal sphincterotomy.
extra: A lateral fissure suggests Crohn's, HIV, syphilis, TB, or cancer.
points: A lateral fissure suggests Crohn's, HIV, syphilis, TB, or cancer.

text: Goodsall's rule: {{anterior}} fistulas track straight; {{posterior}} fistulas curve to the posterior midline.
extra: Exception: anterior openings more than 3 cm from the verge may track posteriorly.
points: Exception: anterior openings more than 3 cm from the verge may track posteriorly.

text: Most common cause of lower GI bleeding in adults: {{diverticulosis}}.
extra: Arterial bleeding, usually stops spontaneously.

text: Ulcerative colitis begins in the {{rectum}} and is continuous and limited to the mucosa.
extra: Associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis and toxic megacolon.
points: Associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis and toxic megacolon.

text: Locally advanced rectal cancer (T3 or node positive) gets {{neoadjuvant chemoradiation}} before total mesorectal excision.
extra: Total neoadjuvant therapy is now common.
points: Total neoadjuvant therapy is now common.

text: Cantlie's line runs from the {{gallbladder fossa to the IVC}}.
extra: It separates right and left liver along the middle hepatic vein.
points: It separates right and left liver along the middle hepatic vein.

text: The Pringle maneuver clamps the {{hepatoduodenal ligament}}.
extra: It occludes portal vein and hepatic artery. Bleeding that continues is from hepatic veins or IVC.
points: It occludes portal vein and hepatic artery.
Bleeding that continues is from hepatic veins or IVC.

text: A replaced right hepatic artery arises from the {{SMA}}.
extra: It runs posterolateral to the common bile duct. A replaced left arises from the left gastric.
points: It runs posterolateral to the common bile duct.
A replaced left arises from the left gastric.

text: Most common benign liver tumor: {{hemangioma}}.
extra: Peripheral nodular enhancement with centripetal fill. Do not biopsy.
points: Peripheral nodular enhancement with centripetal fill.

text: Focal nodular hyperplasia has a {{central stellate scar}} and needs no treatment.
extra: Contains Kupffer cells (takes up sulfur colloid). No malignant potential.
points: Contains Kupffer cells (takes up sulfur colloid).

text: Milan criteria for transplant in HCC: one tumor up to {{5 cm}}, or up to three tumors each up to {{3 cm}}.
extra: No vascular invasion or extrahepatic disease.
points: No vascular invasion or extrahepatic disease.

text: Do not aspirate an {{echinococcal (hydatid)}} cyst.
extra: Risk of anaphylaxis. Albendazole then resection. Amebic abscess: metronidazole.

text: Critical view of safety: only {{two}} structures enter the gallbladder.
extra: Hepatocystic triangle cleared and lower third of the gallbladder off the cystic plate.
points: Hepatocystic triangle cleared and lower third of the gallbladder off the cystic plate.

text: Brown pigment stones form in the {{bile ducts from infection}}.
extra: Black stones: hemolysis and cirrhosis. Cholesterol stones are the most common.
points: Cholesterol stones are the most common.

text: Child-Pugh score components: {{bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites, encephalopathy}}.
extra: MELD uses bilirubin, INR, creatinine, and sodium.
points: MELD uses bilirubin, INR, creatinine, and sodium.

text: Type I choledochal cyst is treated with {{cyst excision and hepaticojejunostomy}}.
extra: Risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Type I (fusiform) is the most common.
points: Type I (fusiform) is the most common.

text: Most common cause of acute pancreatitis in the US: {{gallstones}}, then alcohol.
extra: Cholecystectomy during the same admission for mild gallstone pancreatitis.
points: Cholecystectomy during the same admission for mild gallstone pancreatitis.

text: Tumor marker for pancreatic adenocarcinoma: {{CA 19-9}}; most common mutation: {{KRAS}}.
extra: About 70% arise in the head.

text: In pancreas divisum most drainage goes through the {{minor papilla}}.
extra: Failed fusion of the dorsal and ventral ducts. Duct of Santorini.
points: Failed fusion of the dorsal and ventral ducts.

text: Annular pancreas is treated with {{duodenal bypass}}, not pancreatic resection.
extra: Encircles the second part of the duodenum. Duodenoduodenostomy or duodenojejunostomy.
points: Encircles the second part of the duodenum.

text: Most gastrinomas lie in the gastrinoma triangle; the diagnostic test is {{secretin stimulation}}.
extra: Triangle: cystic-CBD junction, 2nd-3rd duodenum, neck-body of pancreas. Check for MEN1.
points: Triangle: cystic-CBD junction, 2nd-3rd duodenum, neck-body of pancreas.

text: Glucagonoma causes {{necrolytic migratory erythema}}, diabetes, and DVT.
extra: VIPoma: watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria. Somatostatinoma: diabetes, gallstones, steatorrhea.

text: Allow a pancreatic pseudocyst about {{6 weeks}} to mature before internal drainage.
extra: Drain only if symptomatic. Endoscopic cystgastrostomy is first line.

text: Main-duct IPMN is treated with {{resection}}.
extra: Branch-duct IPMN: resect for high-risk features such as size over 3 cm, mural nodule, or jaundice.
points: Branch-duct IPMN: resect for high-risk features such as size over 3 cm, mural nodule, or jaundice.

text: Mucinous cystic neoplasm: middle-aged women, body or tail, {{ovarian-type stroma}}; resect.
extra: Serous cystadenoma is benign with a central scar.
points: Serous cystadenoma is benign with a central scar.

text: Most common complication after a Whipple: {{delayed gastric emptying}}.
extra: Pancreatic leak is the most serious; drain amylase guides diagnosis.
points: Pancreatic leak is the most serious; drain amylase guides diagnosis.

text: Isolated gastric varices from splenic vein thrombosis are treated with {{splenectomy}}.
extra: Usually from chronic pancreatitis. Called sinistral portal hypertension.

text: Most common organism in overwhelming post-splenectomy infection: {{Streptococcus pneumoniae}}.
extra: Highest risk in children and within 2 years of splenectomy.
points: Highest risk in children and within 2 years of splenectomy.

text: Most common site of an accessory spleen: {{splenic hilum}}.
extra: Missing Howell-Jolly bodies after splenectomy suggests one was left.
points: Missing Howell-Jolly bodies after splenectomy suggests one was left.

text: Repair a splenic artery aneurysm if larger than {{2 cm}}, symptomatic, or in a woman of {{childbearing age}}.
extra: Rupture in pregnancy carries high maternal and fetal mortality.
points: Rupture in pregnancy carries high maternal and fetal mortality.

text: Most common indication for elective splenectomy: {{ITP}} that fails medical therapy.
extra: First line is steroids, then IVIG. The spleen is normal in size.
points: First line is steroids, then IVIG.
The spleen is normal in size.

text: Hesselbach's triangle: {{inferior epigastric vessels}}, rectus border, inguinal ligament.
extra: Direct hernias pass through it.

text: Nerve most often injured in open inguinal hernia repair: {{ilioinguinal}}.
extra: Laparoscopic repair: lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (triangle of pain).
points: Laparoscopic repair: lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (triangle of pain).

text: The triangle of doom contains the {{external iliac vessels}}.
extra: Bounded by the vas deferens medially and the gonadal vessels laterally.
points: Bounded by the vas deferens medially and the gonadal vessels laterally.

text: A Richter's hernia traps only the {{antimesenteric wall}} of the bowel.
extra: It can strangulate without obstruction. Littre: Meckel's. Amyand: appendix in an inguinal hernia.
points: Amyand: appendix in an inguinal hernia.

text: Obturator hernia gives the {{Howship-Romberg}} sign: medial thigh pain with internal rotation.
extra: Typical in thin elderly women presenting with bowel obstruction.
points: Typical in thin elderly women presenting with bowel obstruction.

text: A femoral hernia lies {{medial}} to the femoral vein and below the inguinal ligament.
extra: High risk of strangulation. More common in women.

text: A Spigelian hernia passes through the {{linea semilunaris}}, usually below the arcuate line.
extra: It sits deep to the external oblique and is hard to feel.
points: It sits deep to the external oblique and is hard to feel.

text: ABI in claudication is about {{0.5 to 0.9}}; rest pain is under 0.4.
extra: ABI over 1.3 means calcified vessels: use toe pressures.
points: ABI over 1.3 means calcified vessels: use toe pressures.

text: Most common site of lower extremity atherosclerotic occlusion: the {{SFA at the adductor canal}}.
extra: Causes calf claudication.

text: Leriche syndrome: buttock claudication, {{impotence}}, and absent femoral pulses.
extra: Aortoiliac occlusive disease.

text: Most common peripheral aneurysm: {{popliteal}}; repair at {{2 cm}} or if symptomatic.
extra: Half are bilateral; look for AAA. They thrombose or embolize rather than rupture.
points: Half are bilateral; look for AAA.
They thrombose or embolize rather than rupture.

text: Bloody diarrhea after AAA repair means {{ischemic colitis}}; get sigmoidoscopy.
extra: From loss of the IMA. Full-thickness necrosis needs colectomy.

text: An aortoenteric fistula usually involves the {{third or fourth portion of the duodenum}}.
extra: Herald bleed after aortic graft. Treat with graft excision and extra-anatomic bypass or in-situ reconstruction.
points: Treat with graft excision and extra-anatomic bypass or in-situ reconstruction.

text: An SMA embolus lodges distal to the {{middle colic artery}}, sparing proximal jejunum.
extra: Pain out of proportion to exam. Most emboli come from the heart.
points: Pain out of proportion to exam.
Most emboli come from the heart.

text: May-Thurner syndrome: left iliac vein compressed by the {{right iliac artery}}.
extra: Left leg DVT. Treat with thrombolysis and stenting.

text: Symptomatic carotid stenosis of {{50 to 99}}% is an indication for endarterectomy.
extra: Best done within 2 weeks of symptoms. Asymptomatic: consider at 70% or more.
points: Best done within 2 weeks of symptoms.

text: Virchow's triad: {{stasis}}, {{endothelial injury}}, {{hypercoagulability}}.
extra: IVC filter if anticoagulation is contraindicated or has failed.
points: IVC filter if anticoagulation is contraindicated or has failed.

text: Most common lung cancer: {{adenocarcinoma}}.
extra: Peripheral; most common in non-smokers. Squamous is central and makes PTHrP.
points: Squamous is central and makes PTHrP.

text: Small cell lung cancer causes {{SIADH}} and ectopic ACTH.
extra: Central, neuroendocrine, treated mainly with chemoradiation.
points: Central, neuroendocrine, treated mainly with chemoradiation.

text: Pancoast tumor causes {{Horner's syndrome}} and ulnar-distribution pain.
extra: Ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis. Treat with chemoradiation then resection.

text: Predicted postoperative FEV1 should exceed {{0.8 L}} (about 40%) for lung resection.
extra: Below that, further testing with VO2 max.
points: Below that, further testing with VO2 max.

text: Chylothorax: pleural triglycerides above {{110}} mg/dL.
extra: The thoracic duct crosses right to left at T4-5. Conservative care first; ligate if over 1 L/day.
points: The thoracic duct crosses right to left at T4-5.
Conservative care first; ligate if over 1 L/day.

text: Posterior mediastinal masses are usually {{neurogenic tumors}}.
extra: Anterior: thymoma, teratoma, thyroid, lymphoma. Middle: cysts and nodes.

text: Pediatric trauma bolus: crystalloid {{20}} mL/kg; blood {{10}} mL/kg.
extra: Hypotension is a late sign in children.
points: Hypotension is a late sign in children.

text: Most common tracheoesophageal fistula: {{proximal atresia with a distal fistula}} (type C).
extra: Check for VACTERL anomalies. NG tube coils in the pouch.
points: NG tube coils in the pouch.

text: Duodenal atresia shows a {{double bubble}} and is linked to Down syndrome.
extra: Bilious vomiting. Treat with duodenoduodenostomy.

text: Hirschsprung's disease is diagnosed by {{suction rectal biopsy}} showing no ganglion cells.
extra: Failure of neural crest migration. Failure to pass meconium in 48 hours.
points: Failure to pass meconium in 48 hours.

text: Intussusception in a stable child is treated with {{air-contrast enema}}.
extra: Currant jelly stool. Older children and adults: look for a lead point.
points: Older children and adults: look for a lead point.

text: Gastroschisis is to the {{right}} of the cord with {{no}} sac.
extra: Omphalocele: midline with a sac and more associated anomalies.
points: Omphalocele: midline with a sac and more associated anomalies.

text: Most common extracranial solid tumor in children: {{neuroblastoma}}.
extra: Usually under 2 years, crosses the midline, calcifies. Wilms tumor: about 3 years, does not cross.
points: Usually under 2 years, crosses the midline, calcifies.
Wilms tumor: about 3 years, does not cross.

text: Most common congenital diaphragmatic hernia: {{Bochdalek}} (left posterolateral).
extra: Stabilize first; pulmonary hypoplasia and hypertension drive mortality. Morgagni is anterior.
points: Stabilize first; pulmonary hypoplasia and hypertension drive mortality.

text: The Kasai procedure for biliary atresia works best before {{60 days}} of age.
extra: Persistent conjugated jaundice. Many later need transplant.

text: NEC's hallmark radiographic finding is {{pneumatosis intestinalis}}.
extra: Premature infants. Operate for free air or clinical deterioration.
points: Operate for free air or clinical deterioration.

text: Acute rejection is mediated by {{T cells}} and occurs over days to months.
extra: Treat with pulse steroids, then anti-thymocyte globulin.
points: Treat with pulse steroids, then anti-thymocyte globulin.

text: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine inhibit {{calcineurin}}, lowering IL-2.
extra: Both are nephrotoxic. Tacrolimus binds FKBP.

text: Sirolimus inhibits {{mTOR}} and impairs wound healing.
extra: Not nephrotoxic. Mycophenolate inhibits purine synthesis.

text: Most common malignancy after transplant: {{skin cancer (squamous cell)}}.
extra: PTLD is driven by EBV: reduce immunosuppression, rituximab.
points: PTLD is driven by EBV: reduce immunosuppression, rituximab.

text: Most common infection after transplant: {{CMV}}; treat with ganciclovir.
extra: Highest risk: donor positive, recipient negative.
points: Highest risk: donor positive, recipient negative.

text: MELD score uses {{bilirubin, INR, and creatinine}} (plus sodium).
extra: It predicts 90-day mortality and allocates livers.
points: It predicts 90-day mortality and allocates livers.

text: Most common early vascular complication of liver transplant: {{hepatic artery thrombosis}}.
extra: Causes biliary ischemia. Often needs retransplant.

text: Rule of nines: each arm {{9}}%, each leg {{18}}%, front of trunk 18%, back 18%, head 9%.
extra: Perineum 1%. The patient's palm is about 1%.

text: Burn resuscitation urine output target in adults: {{0.5}} mL/kg/h.
extra: Children: 1 mL/kg/h.

text: Mafenide penetrates eschar but causes {{metabolic acidosis}}.
extra: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition; painful. Silver sulfadiazine: neutropenia. Silver nitrate: hyponatremia.

text: Hydrofluoric acid burns are treated with {{calcium gluconate}}.
extra: Topical gel, injection, or intra-arterial. Watch for hypocalcemia and arrhythmia.

text: Carbon monoxide poisoning is treated with {{100% oxygen}}.
extra: Half-life falls from about 5 hours to 1 hour. Pulse oximetry reads falsely normal.
points: Half-life falls from about 5 hours to 1 hour.

text: Squamous cell cancer arising in a chronic burn scar: {{Marjolin's ulcer}}.
extra: Biopsy any chronic non-healing wound.

text: Curling's ulcer follows {{burns}}; Cushing's ulcer follows {{head injury}}.
extra: Both are stress ulcers.

text: Most important prognostic factor in localized melanoma: {{Breslow thickness}}.
extra: Most common type: superficial spreading. Nodular has the worst prognosis.

text: Sarcomas metastasize by blood, most often to the {{lung}}.
extra: Grade is the most important prognostic factor. Biopsy with a core needle or longitudinal incision.
points: Grade is the most important prognostic factor.
Biopsy with a core needle or longitudinal incision.

text: Most common retroperitoneal sarcoma: {{liposarcoma}}.
extra: Most common soft tissue sarcoma in children: rhabdomyosarcoma.
points: Most common soft tissue sarcoma in children: rhabdomyosarcoma.

text: Most common skin cancer: {{basal cell carcinoma}}.
extra: Pearly with rolled borders. Rarely metastasizes.

text: Merkel cell carcinoma is a {{neuroendocrine}} skin cancer linked to a polyomavirus.
extra: Aggressive. Wide excision, sentinel node biopsy, and radiation.
points: Wide excision, sentinel node biopsy, and radiation.

text: Frey's syndrome after parotidectomy involves the {{auriculotemporal}} nerve.
extra: Gustatory sweating from aberrant parasympathetic regrowth to sweat glands.
points: Gustatory sweating from aberrant parasympathetic regrowth to sweat glands.

text: Thyroglossal duct cyst is removed with the {{Sistrunk}} procedure, including the central hyoid.
extra: Midline; moves with tongue protrusion.

text: A second branchial cleft cyst lies along the {{anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid}}.
extra: The most common branchial anomaly.

text: Radical neck dissection removes {{CN XI, the internal jugular vein, and the sternocleidomastoid}}.
extra: A modified radical dissection preserves at least one of these.
points: A modified radical dissection preserves at least one of these.

text: Most common malignant salivary gland tumor: {{mucoepidermoid carcinoma}}.
extra: The smaller the gland, the more likely a tumor is malignant.
points: The smaller the gland, the more likely a tumor is malignant.

text: Doxorubicin causes {{cardiomyopathy}}; bleomycin causes {{pulmonary fibrosis}}.
extra: Cisplatin: kidney, ear, nerve toxicity. Vincristine: neuropathy. Cyclophosphamide: hemorrhagic cystitis.

text: The most radiosensitive phase of the cell cycle is {{M}} phase.
extra: S phase is the most resistant.
points: S phase is the most resistant.

text: Cowden syndrome: {{PTEN}} mutation with hamartomas, breast, thyroid, and endometrial cancer.
extra: Peutz-Jeghers: STK11, hamartomatous polyps and mucocutaneous pigmentation.
points: Peutz-Jeghers: STK11, hamartomatous polyps and mucocutaneous pigmentation.

text: CEA is used for colorectal cancer {{surveillance}}, not screening.
extra: AFP: HCC and germ cell. CA-125: ovarian. Calcitonin: medullary thyroid.

text: Hemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide is prevented with {{mesna}}.
extra: The toxic metabolite is acrolein.

text: Sensitivity = {{TP / (TP + FN)}}.
extra: Specificity = TN / (TN + FP). A sensitive test rules out disease when negative.
points: A sensitive test rules out disease when negative.

text: A type I error is a {{false positive}}: rejecting a true null hypothesis.
extra: Type II error: false negative. Power = 1 minus beta.

text: Number needed to treat = 1 / {{absolute risk reduction}}.
extra: Relative risk reduction overstates benefit when baseline risk is low.
points: Relative risk reduction overstates benefit when baseline risk is low.

text: A case-control study yields an {{odds ratio}}; a cohort study yields a {{relative risk}}.
extra: Case-control starts from the outcome and looks back at exposure.
points: Case-control starts from the outcome and looks back at exposure.

text: Compare the means of two groups with a {{t-test}}; three or more with {{ANOVA}}.
extra: Categorical data: chi-square.

text: In an emergency when the patient cannot consent and no surrogate is available, consent is {{implied}}.
extra: Proceed with life-saving treatment.
